speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: asked the Minister for Education whether the Ministry can provide the respective breakdown on the financial aid per capita that is currently provided to students studying in (i) NUS (ii) Yale-NUS College (iii) Polytechnics (iv) Institute of Technical Education (ITE) and (v) private Universities, such as SIM.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The bursaries are tiered, with a higher level of support extended to those from lower-income households.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: This corresponds to around the bottom 20% by household income.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Institutions also provide their own financial aid to students to further reduce any remaining out-of-pocket expenses and these are typically funded from donations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: In addition to Government and institution bursaries, students have access to Government-funded loans that can be used to pay tuition fees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: These are not means-tested and are interest-free during the course of study and payable only upon graduation or leaving the institution.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: PEI students may apply for financial aid offered by PEIs or tap on education loans offered by commercial banks, to finance their studies.
